units.source_text: 有人说，大竹七段和吴清源六段曾向某心灵学家求教，问赢棋时应持什么态度。

en.t: It is said that Otake, seventh dan, and Go Seigen, sixth dan, once sought advice from a certain spiritualist, asking what attitude one should have when winning a game.

units.source_text: 心灵学家回答说：在对手思考时，最好仍是专心致志。

en.t: The spiritualist replied: while your opponent is thinking, it is still best to remain completely focused.

units.source_text: 据说曾列席观看本因坊名人告别赛的小野田六段在几年之后，即在他死前不久，

en.t: It is said that Onoda, sixth dan, who had been present to watch the Honinbo master's farewell match, a few years later, shortly before his own death,

units.source_text: 不仅在日本棋院举办的升段赛中大获全胜，棋艺的高超也令人瞠目而视。

en.t: not only won every game in a promotion tournament held by the Nihon Ki-in, but also astonished people with the brilliance of his play.

units.source_text: 对局的态度确实非同凡响。

en.t: His attitude during play was truly extraordinary.

units.source_text: 对手下子的时候，他静静地瞑目养神，仿佛摆脱了获胜的欲望。

en.t: When his opponent placed a stone, he would quietly close his eyes and rest his spirit, as if freed from the desire to win.

units.source_text: 升段赛结束后，他便住进了医院，自己还不知道是得了胃癌，就去世了。

en.t: After the promotion tournament ended, he entered the hospital and died without even knowing himself that he had stomach cancer.

units.source_text: 大竹七段少年时代的恩师久保松六段也在死前的升段赛中取得了优异的成绩。

en.t: Kubomatsu, sixth dan, who had been Otake's teacher in his youth, also achieved excellent results in a promotion tournament before his death.
